thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: p99 latency > 2.5s for dedicated-prod eu-west-1 (streaming endpoints). Alerts: p99 streaming stalls, queue depth rising. Auto-escalate to #incidents and @sre-oncall.
ryan: saw the alert. p95 also drifting. Is this the warmup/coldpool thing?
maya: looks like dedicated pool in eu-west-1 saturated. Autoscaler reports scale-up requests queued for ~45s. Warmup completions are slow.
ash: (adding logs) from autoscaler: `scale_action_id=ac-9981 state=initiated -> provisioning -> handshake_wait` then `handshake_timeout` for some nodes.
sre-oncall: paging in. I'm on it. tagging eng-runtime and ops. @eng-runtime-lead can you join?
eng-runtime-lead: joining. summary pls — are customers seeing errors or just higher latency?
support-lead: support is getting multiple tickets for streaming stalls (clients report connections freeze then reconnect, sometimes partial responses). No 5xx spikes in hosted layer yet. Several high-value customers on dedicated pools are affected.
ryan: metrics: queue_depth (dedicated-eu-west-1) spiked from 20->450 in 7m. streaming_error_rate up from 0.2% -> 2.7%. p99 streaming latency hitting 6-8s intermittently.
maya: root cause hypothesis: autoscaler handshake/warmup slower due to image pull congestion + KV-cache cold path amplification when many long-live streams spin up concurrently. Lots of cold KV loads + token-heavy requests.
ops: confirming container images pulled from our internal registry had elevated latency for eu-west-1 in the last 30m (registry slow). That would delay warmup.
eng-runtime-lead: ok — immediate actions: 1) start manual scale-up of reserved pool to absorb queue; 2) enable temporary queue-throttling to protect tail; 3) reroute a subset of traffic to fallback model variant (lower mem/quant) for degraded latency.
sre-oncall: executing 1) manual scale: `rm scale --pool dedicated-eu-west-1 --count +8 --reason "incident 7912345678 manual absorb"` (running)
incidents-bot: Change recorded: manual scale +8 by sre-oncall. Estimated ready ~45s.
ash: while nodes come up, can we force KV-cache warm fill for top prefixes? we have a warmup job we used previously.
eng-runtime-lead: good call. launching warmup job against the new nodes and existing ones. snippet: ```
# warmup quick
curl -X POST https://internal-warmup/api/warm --data '{"model":"gpt-like","prefixes":["Hello","Summarize","Translate"]}'
```
ryan: started warmup. hit logs show warmup tasks accepted. queue depth starting to drop from 450 -> 220. p99 still elevated but trending.
support-lead: customer-impact update: we've messaged top 3 affected accounts; none have disconnected yet but some report degraded UX. asking for ETA and mitigation steps.
ops: registry latency is improving after scale on registry side (~10m ago). image pull times back to baseline. autoscaler handshake failure rate dropping in metrics.
maya: autoscaler backlog metric still shows ~2 queued scale requests. We should pause automatic scaling to avoid additional unstable churn while we stabilize.
sre-oncall: pausing autoscaler for eu-west-1 now: `autoscaler pause --region eu-west-1 --reason "stabilize after handshake flaps"`
incidents-bot: Autoscaler paused for eu-west-1 by sre-oncall.
eng-runtime-lead: next steps: keep manual scaling until queues < 50 for 10m. Keep warmup job running for 15m. Gradually unpause autoscaler once handshake success rate > 95% for 5m. Also add temporary routing rule to divert 20% non-critical traffic to dedicated-fallback-quantized to reduce hotshot pressure.
nash: adding the routing rule now. `route update --pool=dedicated-eu-west-1 --divert 20% --target=dedicated-eu-west-1-fallback`
ryan: diversion in place. seeing immediate p99 improvement on diverted subset (~1.8s). main pool still at ~3.2-4s but improving. queue depth down to 90.
support-lead: messaging customers with ETA 25m and steps we're taking. they appreciated the quick update.
maya: note to follow-up: capture autoscaler handshake logs and correlate with registry latency and node-init times. Might need longer term: staggered warmup, pre-warm hotshot spots, or softer autoscaler backoff.
sre-oncall: assigning a follow-up ticket: INCIDENT-7912345678-rootcause to eng-runtime and ops for postmortem. I'll remain until unpause.
eng-runtime-lead: agree. I'll collect runtime traces and timeline. ops, please send registry metrics + mitigation timeline.
ops: acked, I'll assemble artifact links.
ryan: final quick check — p99 now 1.6s for diverted, 2.4s for pool overall, streaming error rate back to 0.4%, queue depth steady ~28.
incidents-bot: Incident active -> mitigated (partial). Next action: postmortem in 24h required.
support-lead: closing customer loop with summary and offer credits as needed.
eng-runtime-lead: leaving note: consider adding pre-pull for images for scheduled large campaigns and improve autoscaler handshake backoff. will include recommendations in postmortem.
sre-oncall: handing back to oncall rotation (sre-oncall -> ops). If anything regresses ping #incidents immediately. :thumbsup:
